title: Weighted-span selector and triage assistant for ops context
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Build a service-level component (Triage Assistant) that consumes trace/span telemetry and associated logs/metrics to produce a compact, ranked evidence bundle for on-call workflows. The assistant will select representative spans (weighted by error rate, latency contribution, and user impact), synthesize a short natural-language brief, attach a minimal set of logs and KPIs, and surface an ordered list of suggested runbook actions. Output destinations: PagerDuty incident payloads, Slack incident threads, and the Console incident sidebar.

Goals:
- Reduce mean time to investigative context by providing a single-click ‘evidence snapshot’ attached to alerts.
- Prioritize signals so juniors see the most actionable context first (e.g., root span with the highest p95 delta, accompanying error logs, and impacted customer count).
- Maintain small payload sizes (<= 500KB for PD/Slack attachments), with links to the full artifact in Console.
- Be conservative with sensitive data: scrub PII/keys and respect tenant data retention/KMS policies.

Design notes and heuristics:
- Input sources: sampled traces (OpenTelemetry spans), metrics (prometheus/cortex), and correlated logs (ELK/Cloud logging).
- Weighting scheme: score spans by a combination of (a) span error flag * 5, (b) delta to baseline latency percentile * 3, (c) request volume impact fraction * 2, (d) presence of downstream service failures * 2. Weights are configurable via runtime flags.
- Selection window: default 10-minute window around alerting signal. Support configurable windows per alert policy.
- Representative span selection: after scoring, select top-3 distinct traces ensuring diversity (different trace root IDs and covering multi-service call graphs). For each trace include: top span, span timeline snippet (3 hops), selected annotated logs (max 10 lines total), and a tiny flamegraph thumbnail (pre-rendered SVG).
- Brief synthesis: use a lightweight template-based summarizer (no LLM to begin with) that fills slots (symptom, probable subsystem, impact estimate, suggested runbook steps). Future iteration: optional LLM enrichment behind an opt-in flag.
- Attachments: produce two payload formats: PD-compact (payload JSON + single URL to Console snapshot) and Slack-rich (thread starter with blocks and Console snapshot link). Console snapshot stores the full artifact bundle and an audit trail.

Acceptance criteria:
- When enabled on an alert policy, the assistant attaches a PD compact payload within 8s of alert ingestion for 95% of events under normal load.
- Slack thread starter shows short brief + 3 inline indicators (top span id, p95 delta, impacted tenant count) and a Console link.
- Generated bundles are <500KB for PD/Slack attachments in 99% of cases; remainder is preserved via Console link.
- PII filter runs on all logs included; no raw request bodies or obvious tokens are included.
- End-to-end tests exercise a synthetic high-latency trace, verify selection logic, and assert attachment payload shape.

Implementation plan:
1) Proto: implement offline selection utility in obs/triage-service that reads sample traces and returns a JSON candidate bundle (2w sprint).
2) PD/Slack integrations: extend existing incident webhook composer to accept triage bundle and generate PD/Slack payloads (1w).
3) Console snapshot store: API + object storage + short-lived signed link generator (2w).
4) CI tests: unit tests for scoring, integration test with a traffic generator producing synthetic traces and logs, and load test at 2x normal alert QPS (1w).
5) Rollout: opt-in feature flag behind policy setting -> limited pilot with Platform SRE team -> broader enablement.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Running selection real-time vs async: real-time keeps PD latency low but requires fast sampling and compute; async reduces compute but increases attachment latency. Implementation chosen: near-real-time with small worker pool and a short per-alert timeout (default 8s).
- LLM enrichment is powerful but introduces cost, latency, and data residency concerns. Defer to later opt-in stage behind private deployment guardrails.
- Sensitive data leakage: risk mitigated by a strict scrubber using regex + allowlists, plus per-tenant data policy enforcement. Security review required if we enable request bodies or stack traces with file paths.

Testing and observability:
- Add metrics: triage.bundle.generated_total, triage.bundle.size_bytes.histogram, triage.bundle.latency_ms.histogram, triage.bundle.scrubbed_total, triage.bundle.errors_total.
- Dashboards: triage health panel in Console showing generation success rate, avg size, and top failure modes.
- Alerting: if bundle generation error rate >5% over 15m, create an ops incident to a PD routing key for infra-sre.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: deploy triage worker to staging, run synthetic tests.
- Week 1: pilot with Platform SRE team on non-prod alert policies. Collect qualitative feedback and iterate.
- Week 2: enable for 10% of production alert policies (flagged), monitor metrics.
- Week 3: enable for all infra-sre policies, provide self-serve toggle in alerting policy UI.

Open questions:
- Should the assistant surface suggested rollback actions automatically or only link to runbook steps? (Security and product decision.)
- Do we allow customer-supplied runbook snippets to be pulled into the brief? (consent/privacy consideration)
- What retention policy for Console snapshots is appropriate by default? Proposed 30 days for snapshots, configurable per-org.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Triage+Assistant+Design
- Proto repo: https://git.redwood.com/obs/triage-service (branch: feature/triage-assistant)
- Console snapshot API PR: https://git.redwood.com/console/pulls/1824
- Synthetic test harness: https://git.redwood.com/obs/test-harness/commits/ci/triage-sim
- Dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/triage-assistant-health

Backlog tasks (follow-ups):
- Add tenant-aware scrubbing rules UI in Console.
- Implement optional LLM-based brief enrichment (planner ticket).
- Add fallback strategy to include last-known good config and recent deploy metadata in the snapshot.
- Support automatic creation of a Postmortem draft if incident severity >= P1 and triage bundle suggests a config regression.
acceptance_criteria: PD payload attached within 8s for 95% of alerts under normal load
Slack thread starter includes brief + top span + p95 delta + impacted count + Console link
Attachments < 500KB in 99% of cases; full bundle accessible from Console link
PII scrubber blocks request bodies and tokens from attachments
E2E synthetic test verifies selection correctness and payload schema
comments: 2026-02-26 - Maya Chen: Spike complete. Implemented scoring prototype and ran it against last 7 days of sampled traces. Top-k selection looks stable; average bundle size ~320KB after log trimming.

2026-03-02 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented initial worker and PD payload composer. Hitting PD payload size limit in some cases; added step to offload full bundle to Console and use compact PD payload with link.

2026-03-05 - Platform SRE (review): Requested stricter scrub rules for stack traces and removal of local file paths. Also asked for a config toggle to disable including span-level logs for specific tenants.
2026-03-09 - UX (review): Suggested adding a one-line TL;DR at the top of the Slack block to help rapid scannability. Also requested an expandable view in Console snapshot to show full flamegraph.
2026-03-13 - Diego Alvarez: Load test results: at 2x alert QPS worker latency p95 = 2200ms, success rate 97%. Plan to increase worker pool and add circuit-breaker for high-latency conditions.
